name: Question 5
problem:
| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.5$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |

Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{80}$ be a random sample of size $n=80$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is greater than $0.1.$

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=80,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =-1\cdot 0.3+0\cdot 0.5+1\cdot 0.1+2\cdot 0.1 \\  & =-0.3+0+0.1+0.3 \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =((-1)^{2}\cdot 0.3+{0}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{1}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.1)-{0}^{2} \\  & =(0.3+0+0.1+0.4)-0 \\  & =0.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0,\frac{0.8}{80}) \\  & ∼N(0,0.01).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>0.1).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>0.1) & ≈P(Z>\frac{0.1-0}{\sqrt{0.01}}) \\  & =P(Z>1) \\  & =1-Φ(1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(\overset{―}{X}>0.1)=1-Φ(1).
$$

EXPLANATION

Suppose that X1,X2,…,Xn is a random sample of size n from a population with population mean μ and population standard deviation σ. The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large n, the distribution of the sample mean X― can be approximated as

X―∼N(μ,σ2n).

In our case:

  • the sample size is n=80,

  • the population mean is μ=E[X]=∑i=1nxif(xi)=−1⋅0.3+0⋅0.5+1⋅0.1+2⋅0.1=−0.3+0+0.1+0.3=0,

  • the population variance is σ2=Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=((−1)2⋅0.3+02⋅0.5+12⋅0.1+22⋅0.1)−02=(0.3+0+0.1+0.4)−0=0.8.

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

X―∼N(μ,σ2n)∼N(0,0.880)∼N(0,0.01).

We want to find P(X―>0.1). So, we convert X― to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(X―>0.1)≈P(Z>0.1−00.01)=P(Z>1)=1−Φ(1).

Therefore, we conclude that

P(X―>0.1)=1−Φ(1).
